title: N-2 ascends along a finite extension of Noetherian domains
statement: Let $A\subseteq B$ be integral domains such that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Then $B$ is N-2: for every finite field extension $M$ [def-pc-field-extension] of the fraction field of $B$, the integral closure of $B$ in $M$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $B$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), in the case of a finite extension named there ('quasi-finite extension of domains (for example finite)'); its proof, second paragraph ('Assume $R\subset S$ ... moreover that $S$ is finite over $R$ ... we win by Lemma integral-permanence'), lines 45225-45232

proof.text: *Fraction fields.* Let $K=A_{(0)}$ and $L=B_{(0)}$ be the fraction fields of $A$ and $B$, their localizations at the prime $(0)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $A\subseteq B\subseteq L$ and every nonzero $s\in A$ is nonzero in the field $L$, the map $\iota:K\to L$, $a/s\mapsto as^{-1}$, is well defined ($a/s=a'/s'$ means $as'=a's$ in the domain $A$, hence in $L$), a ring homomorphism, and injective since $K$ is a field; on $A$ it is the inclusion $A\subseteq B\subseteq L$. So $L$ is a field extension of $K$ through $\iota$ [def-pc-field-extension], and for any field extension $M$ of $L$ the two $A$-algebra structures on $M$, through $A\subseteq K\xrightarrow{\iota}L\subseteq M$ and through $A\subseteq B\subseteq L\subseteq M$, agree.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, first paragraph, lines 45208-45209: 'Let $L/K$ be the induced extension of fraction fields.'

proof.text: *$L/K$ is finite.* Let $b_1,\dots,b_n$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $V=\iota(K)b_1+\dots+\iota(K)b_n\subseteq L$, the $K$-subspace spanned by the $b_i$. Every element $\iota(a/s)\,b$ with $a,s\in A$, $s\ne0$, $b\in B$ lies in $V$: write $ab=\sum_i a_ib_i$ with $a_i\in A$, so $\iota(a/s)b=\sum_i\iota(a_i/s)b_i$. Conversely every element of $V$ is a finite sum of such products, and sums and products of such products are again sums of such products ($\iota(k)b\cdot\iota(k')b'=\iota(kk')bb'$); so $V$ is a subring of $L$ containing $\iota(K)$ and $B$, i.e. a commutative $K$-algebra, an integral domain (a subring of a field), and finite-dimensional over $K$ (spanned by $b_1,\dots,b_n$). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] $V$ is a field. Hence for $b,b'\in B$ with $b'\ne0$ the inverse of $b'$ in $V$, which is its inverse in $L$, lies in $V$, and $b/b'=b\,b'^{-1}\in V$. Every element of $L=B_{(0)}$ has this form, so $V=L$ and $\dim_KL\le n$: $L/K$ is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. (In the source this is the finiteness of $L/K$, obtained there for quasi-finite extensions from Lemma 00PK (2) on the fibre $S\otimes_RK$; in the finite case the fibre $V\cong K\otimes_AB$ is spanned by the images of the $b_i$, and the argument above is that case written out.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, first paragraph, lines 45209-45212: 'Note that this is a finite field extension (for example by Lemma isolated-point-fibre (2) applied to the fibre $S\otimes_R K$ ...)', in the finite case

proof.text: *$M/K$ is finite.* Let $M$ be a finite field extension of $L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. By steps 1 and 2, $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ (through $\iota$) with $L/K$ and $M/L$ finite, so by the tower law [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] $M/K$ is finite, with $[M:K]=[M:L][L:K]$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, second paragraph, lines 45226-45228: 'Let $M$ be a finite field extension of the fraction field of $S$. Then $M$ is also a finite field extension of $K$'

proof.text: *The closure of $A$.* Let $T_A\subseteq M$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $M$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], $M$ being an $A$-algebra through $A\subseteq K\to M$, which by step 1 is the same as through $A\subseteq B\subseteq M$. Since $A$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] and $M/K$ is finite (step 3), $T_A$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, second paragraph, lines 45228-45229: 'and we conclude that the integral closure $T$ of $R$ in $M$ is finite over $R$'

proof.text: *$T_A$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $M$.* Let $T_B\subseteq M$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $M$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. (a) $T_A\subseteq T_B$: if $x\in M$ satisfies $x^m+a_{m-1}x^{m-1}+\dots+a_0=0$ with $a_i\in A$, this is a monic equation with coefficients $a_i\in A\subseteq B$, so $x$ is integral over $B$. (b) $T_B\subseteq T_A$: $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, so $B$ is integral over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] $T_B$ is a subring of $M$ containing $B$, and each of its elements is integral over $B$, i.e. the ring map $B\to T_B$ is integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] applied to $A\to B\to T_B$, every $x\in T_B$ is integral over $A$, i.e. $x\in T_A$. Hence $T_A=T_B$. This is the case of Algebra, Lemma 0308 (lemma-integral-closure-transitive, line 7723) used by the source, for $A\to B\to M$, where the integral closure of $A$ in $B$ is all of $B$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, second paragraph, lines 45229-45230: 'By Lemma integral-closure-transitive [Tag 0308] we see that $T$ is also the integral closure of $S$ in $M$'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Let $t_1,\dots,t_m$ generate $T_A$ as an $A$-module (step 4). Since $T_B=T_A$ (step 5) and $A\subseteq B$, every $A$-linear combination $\sum_j a_jt_j$ is a $B$-linear combination, so $t_1,\dots,t_m$ generate $T_B$ as a $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (Algebra, Lemma 02JM (2): $A\to C$ finite implies $B\to C$ finite, for $C=T_B$). As $M$ was an arbitrary finite field extension of the fraction field $L$ of $B$, $B$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. (The hypothesis that $A$ is Noetherian is not used in this finite case; the source needs it only for the reduction of quasi-finite extensions to finite ones.)
